title: Assessing the Impact of a University Transition Online Course on Student Continuation Using Statistical Matching Methods
reason: Propensity-matched comparison of first-year pass rates by binary enrolment in an optional online transition course. Authors state no engagement or completion data were available; enrolment is treatment membership, not an activity indicator.

extraction.design: quasi-experimental (propensity score matching, doubly robust estimation)
extraction.n_quote: Given our large sample size (n = 28,372), our study was well-powered to detect even small
extraction.lms_indicators: none (binary enrolment in the online course only)
extraction.notes: ATET 6.2 percentage points is a treatment (enrolment) effect, not an indicator-outcome relation. Authors: 'our analysis is based solely on a binary indicator of enrolment, which does not capture the degree of students’ engagement or course completion.'
